newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends sharply lower in consolidation.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends sharply lower in consolidation.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures pulled back sharply on Monday, in a technical correction to the market's recent uptrend, traders said.
"The market looked tired and a little overdone," said Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes.

Key March delivery fell 2.20 cents per lb on the day, to settle at 114.05 cents, after ranging between 116.25 and 113.60. Second-position May ended 1.90 cents lower, at 112.45 cents, while the outer months closed down 1.40 to 2.30.
Volume reached an estimated at 5,300 lots.

Prices headed lower at the outset on speculative and local selling. The most-active March contract breached key chart support at 115.25-115.00 cents per lb and touched off sell-stops below that level.
Scale-down trade buying limited losses, preventing the March contract from testing the next level of support at 113.00-112.50 cents, dealers said.
Merrill Lynch's Ganes expects the market to continue to come under pressure as increased availability of coffee prompts producer sales.
She said while the cold snap in Europe could help to increase coffee consumption there, mild temperatures in the eastern U.S. were likely to offset demand overseas.

Traders also said anticipation of a substantial increase in speculative (non-commercial and nonreportable) long positions ahead of the release of the CFTC Commitment of Traders Report may have also weighed on the market.
The biweekly report for the weeks ended December 24 and December 31 will be issued this afternoon after 1530 EST (2030 GMT).
The CSCE certified coffee stock figures are also due later today. Last week, the CSCE reported stocks were unchanged in the week ended Dec. 27 at 34,065 bags.
Traders are keeping an eye on the weather in Brazil, where heavy rains have left over 60 people dead and thousands homeless.
Coffee trees in Brazil's key growing state of Minas Gerais have escaped damage, although growers said the rains prevented the application of pesticides against insects.
